direction: Hybridize the two strongest full-completion 500 ms TSP constructive rules: the O(n^2) vectorized linear endpoint pull 0.7*d(dest,u) - d(cur,u) (T69 dest-pull) with the unvisited mean-farness isolation term (T46), both rescaled by a dimensionless per-step normalization so the score is invariant to coordinate scale. Target: keep T69's sub-millisecond 128/128 completion while capturing T46's better relative gap, i.e. move the speed-quality Pareto knee rather than chase O(n^4) rollout quality.

operations.mechanism: KB evidence: dest-pull (T69) achieves 128/128 completion at 0.63 ms median with mean_rel_gap 0.1555 (EoH-128) and 0.1649 (TSPLIB 18) via the single vectorized expression argmax_u (0.7*d(dest,u) - d(cur,u)); mean-farness (T46) reaches the best gap among full-completion rules (+0.1428 / +0.1445) using an unvisited-isolation pull; dimensionless-ratio (T81) shows all features normalized by per-step maxima are scale-invariant and still 128/128 complete. T1 step-rollout shows the quality ceiling but times out (44/128), so the budget-safe route is to blend cheap O(n^2) features instead of lookahead. Sandbox limitation: the globals() probe was rejected by the AST whitelist, so feature verification is deferred to diagnose_suite inside this evolution round.

preserve: Route feasibility, strict time budget, and scale invariance.
hypothesis: If selection score combines step-normalized endpoint attraction (dest-pull) with a step-normalized mean-farness isolation term, then the constructive tour gap decreases versus pure dest-pull at equal O(n^2) cost (sub-millisecond per instance, 100% completion under 500 ms), because the isolation term prevents the tour from stranding far-from-all-unvisited cities for late expensive closure, while normalization keeps the mix robust across distance scales.
